ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p212/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p212/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p212/r5.claim: Zamakhshari coordinates ‘cast your staff’ with ‘blessed,’ supplying an implied ‘he was told’ and citing the repeated explanatory particle in the parallel wording.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p212/r5.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: فإن قلت: علام عطف قوله: وألق عصاك؟ قلت: على بورك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p212/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p212/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p212/r6.claim: Abu Hayyan rejects Zamakhshari’s coordination and says the command is a sentence coordinated with the preceding declarative ‘I am God’; such mixed coordination is permitted.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p212/r6.anchor: بل قوله: وألق عصاك معطوف على قوله: إنه أنا الله العزيز الحكيم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p212/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p212/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p212/r7.claim: The omitted step after the staff began trembling is that Moses cast it from his hand.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p212/r7.anchor: فلما رآها تهتز: ثم محذوف تقديره: فألقاها من يده

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p212/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p212/r8.speaker: الحسن، والزهري، وعمرو بن عبيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p212/r8.claim: These readers pronounce ‘jān’ with hamza instead of alif, apparently to avoid two consecutive sukūns; Abu Hayyan notes a parallel hamza reading by Amr ibn Ubayd.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p212/r8.anchor: وقرأ الحسن، والزهري، وعمرو بن عبيد: جأن، بهمزة مكان الألف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p212/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p212/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p212/r9.claim: The snake’s appearance is a change in attributes and qualities, not destruction of the staff’s substance followed by creation of a snake.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p212/r9.anchor: وليس إعداما لذاتها وخلقها لحية وثعبان، بل ذلك من تغيير الصفات لا تغيير الذات

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p212/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p212/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p212/r10.claim: Calling it a jān compares its rapid, restless movement to a small snake while preserving its large body.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p212/r10.anchor: شبهها بها في سرعة اضطرابها وحركتها، مع عظم جثتها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p212/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p212/r11.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p212/r11.claim: Mujahid glosses ‘without looking back’ as Moses not returning.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p212/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p212/r12.speaker: السدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p212/r12.claim: Al-Suddi glosses it as Moses not lingering.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p212/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p212/r13.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p212/r13.claim: Qatada glosses it as Moses not turning around.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p212/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p212/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p212/r14.claim: The verb ‘ʿaqiba’ means to turn toward something one had left, as if returning on one’s heels; it is also used of a fighter who charges again after flight.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p212/r14.anchor: يقال: عقب الرجل: توجه إلى شيء كان ولى عنه، كأنه انصرف على عقبيه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p213/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p213/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p213/r1.claim: Moses’ flight is a natural human response to an extremely terrifying sight: the staff became a moving snake, and no reassurance preceded the sight.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p213/r1.anchor: ولحقه ما لحق طبع البشرية إذا رأى الإنسان أمرا هائلا جدا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p213/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p213/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p213/r2.claim: Zamakhshari says Moses fled because he thought the snake signaled danger, citing the assurance that messengers do not fear in God’s presence.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p213/r2.anchor: قال الزمخشري: وإنما رغب لظنه أن ذلك لأمر أريد به

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p213/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p213/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p213/r3.claim: Ibn Atiyya reads the address as comfort and strength for Moses: God’s chosen messengers fear none but Him; Moses took the snake, which turned back into a staff, and this became habitual.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p213/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: وناداه الله تعالى مؤنسا ومقويا على الأمر: يا موسى لا تخف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p213/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p213/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p213/r4.claim: One interpretation limits the messengers’ lack of fear to the place where revelation comes, although they are the people most fearful of God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p213/r4.anchor: وقيل: المعنى لا يخاف المرسلون في الموضع الذي يوحى إليه فيه، وهم أخوف الناس من الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p213/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p213/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p213/r5.claim: Another interpretation says a messenger should not fear when ordered to display a miracle, though he necessarily fears God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p213/r5.anchor: وقيل: إذا أمرتهم بإظهار معجز، فينبغي أن لا يخافوا فيما يتعلق بإظهار ذلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p213/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p213/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p213/r6.claim: Abu Hayyan prefers an unconnected exception in ‘except one who wronged’: it means ‘but someone other than them who wronged,’ since prophets are protected from such wrong.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p213/r6.anchor: والأظهر أن قوله: إلا من ظلم، استثناء منقطع، والمعنى: لكن من ظلم غيرهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p213/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p213/r7.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p213/r7.claim: Al-Farra and others take the exception as connected but from omitted clauses, meaning that others fear, except the wrongdoer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p213/r7.anchor: وعن الفراء: إنه استثناء متصل من جمل محذوفة، والتقدير: وإنما يخاف غيرهم إلا من ظلم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p213/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p213/r8.speaker: النحاس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p213/r8.claim: Al-Nahhas rejects deriving a connected exception from omitted clauses as impossible and contrary to clear explanation, illustrating with an absurd ‘I strike the people except Zayd’ reading.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p213/r8.anchor: ورده النحاس وقال: الاستثناء من محذوف محال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p213/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p213/r9.speaker: فرقة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p213/r9.claim: A group says ‘except’ means ‘and’; Abu Hayyan rejects this because conjunction includes whereas exception excludes, so the particles are far apart in meaning.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p213/r9.anchor: وقالت فرقة: إلا بمعنى الواو، والتقدير: ولا من ظلم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p213/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p213/r10.speaker: الحسن، ومقاتل، وابن جريج، والضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p213/r10.claim: Reports from Hasan, Muqatil, Ibn Jurayj, and al-Dahhak imply a connected exception.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p213/r10.anchor: وروي عن الحسن، ومقاتل، وابن جريج، والضحاك، ما يقتضي أنه استثناء متصل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p213/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p213/r11.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p213/r11.claim: Ibn Atiyya says scholars agree prophets are protected from major sins and vile minor sins, while disagreeing about other cases; this may explain Hasan’s and Ibn Jurayj’s interpretation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p213/r11.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وأجمع العلماء على أن الأنبياء عليهم الصلاة والسلام معصومون من الكبائر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p213/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p213/r12.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p213/r12.claim: Zamakhshari takes ‘except’ as ‘but’: messengers may have committed a minor lapse, citing Adam, Jonah, David, Solomon, Joseph’s brothers, and Moses striking the Copt; he sees a subtle allusion to Moses.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p213/r12.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: وإلا بمعنى لكن، لأنه لما أطلق نفي الخوف عن المرسل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p213/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p213/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p213/r13.claim: The verse’s exception discussion concerns whether a lapse is compatible with prophetic protection; Abu Hayyan’s preferred disconnected reading avoids attributing such wrongdoing to the messengers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p213/r13.anchor: إذ الأنبياء معصومون من وقوع الظلم الواقع من غيرهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p214/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p214/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p214/r1.claim: Zamakhshari supports his allusion to Moses’ lapse with Moses’ prayer asking forgiveness after saying he wronged himself.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p214/r1.anchor: رب إني ظلمت نفسي فاغفر لي

STUDYQURAN:27:intro/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:27:intro/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:27:intro/r4.claim: The account then recounts Moses encountering fire on the mountain, where God charged him to go to Pharaoh and free the Israelites.
STUDYQURAN:27:intro/r4.anchor: turns to Moses’ encounter with the fire on the mountain, from which God spoke charging him with his mission

RAZI-FULL:v24p158/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p158/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p158/r1.claim: “Throw down your staff” is coordinated with the blessing announcement in 27:8; both clauses explain the call to Moses.
RAZI-FULL:v24p158/r1.anchor: وأن ألق عصاك ، كلاهما تفسير لنودي

RAZI-FULL:v24p158/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p158/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p158/r2.claim: Jānn is a small snake, named so because it hides itself from people.
RAZI-FULL:v24p158/r2.anchor: سميت جانا ، لأنها تستتر عن الناس

RAZI-FULL:v24p158/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p158/r3.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v24p158/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads jānn without tanwīn, following a dialect that avoids the meeting of two sukūns, as in “shaʾba” and “daʾba.”
RAZI-FULL:v24p158/r3.anchor: وقرأ الحسن { جان } على لغة من يهرب من التقاء الساكنين

RAZI-FULL:v24p158/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p158/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p158/r4.claim: Lam yuʿaqqib means he did not return; the idiom describes a fighter turning back after fleeing.
RAZI-FULL:v24p158/r4.anchor: معناه لم يرجع ، يقال عقب المقاتل

RAZI-FULL:v24p158/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p158/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p158/r5.claim: Moses fled because he thought the snake’s appearance meant something was intended against him.
RAZI-FULL:v24p158/r5.anchor: وإنما خاف لظنه أن ذلك لأمر أريد به

RAZI-FULL:v24p158/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p158/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p158/r6.claim: One interpretation limits the messengers’ lack of fear to the occasions when God commands them to display a miracle; otherwise a messenger can certainly feel fear.
RAZI-FULL:v24p158/r6.anchor: وقال بعضهم : المراد إني إذا أمرتهم بإظهار معجز في

BURSEVI:v6p234#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p234#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p234#3/r1.claim: The command to throw the staff is coordinated with the announcement of blessing: Moses was called both to the blessed site and to throw it.
BURSEVI:v6p234#3/r1.anchor: عطف على بورك أي نودي أن بورك من في النار وأن ألق عصاك.

BURSEVI:v6p234#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p234#3/r2.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v6p234#3/r2.claim: One who hears the Real’s call and witnesses beauty casts away every support but God and relies only on divine grace and generosity.
BURSEVI:v6p234#3/r2.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : يشير إلى أن من سمع نداء الحق وشاهد أنوار جماله يلقى من يد همته كل ما كان متوكأه غير الله

BURSEVI:v6p234#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p234#3/r3.speaker: المثنوي
BURSEVI:v6p234#3/r3.claim: A Persian couplet warns that relying on anything besides God’s grace is disbelief along the path.
BURSEVI:v6p234#3/r3.anchor: تكيه برغير خدا كفريست از كفر طريق جز بفضل حق مكن تكيه درين ره اي رفيق

BURSEVI:v6p234#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p234#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p234#3/r4.claim: The fa explains an omitted sequence: Moses threw the staff, it became a moving serpent, and then he saw it shake.
BURSEVI:v6p234#3/r4.anchor: الفاء فصيحة تفصح عن جملة محذوفة كأنه قيل : فألقاها فانقلبت حية تسعى فلما أبصرها

BURSEVI:v6p234#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p234#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p234#3/r5.claim: The serpent moved violently and darted in every direction.
BURSEVI:v6p234#3/r5.anchor: {كأنها جان} حية خفيفة سريعة فشبه الحية العظيمة المسماة

BURSEVI:v6p234#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p234#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p234#3/r6.claim: The comparison is to a light, swift snake called a jann: the large serpent resembles it in speed and twisting motion.
BURSEVI:v6p234#3/r6.anchor: حية خفيفة سريعة فشبه الحية العظيمة المسماة بالفارسية (ادها) بالجان في سرعة الحركة والالتواء

BURSEVI:v6p234#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p234#3/r7.speaker: القاموس
BURSEVI:v6p234#3/r7.claim: Al-Qāmūs describes the jann as a dark-eyed, harmless snake, often found around houses.
BURSEVI:v6p234#3/r7.anchor: والجان ضرب من الحيات أي حية كحلاء العين لا تؤذي كثيرة في الدور كما في "القاموس".

BURSEVI:v6p234#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p234#3/r8.speaker: أبو الليث
BURSEVI:v6p234#3/r8.claim: Abū al-Layth says the thʿubān was the sign before Pharaoh, while the jann appeared at the mountain.
BURSEVI:v6p234#3/r8.anchor: وقال أبو الليث : الصحيح أن الثعبان كان عند فرعون والجان عند الطور

BURSEVI:v6p234#3/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p234#3/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p234#3/r9.claim: The staff’s transformation signals that every support besides God is, in reality, a serpent.
BURSEVI:v6p234#3/r9.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى أن كل متوكأ غير الله في الصورة ثعبان له في المعنى

BURSEVI:v6p234#3/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p234#3/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p234#3/r10.claim: He cites the Mathnawī’s couplet that every fantasy made a home in the heart will take visible form at resurrection.
BURSEVI:v6p234#3/r10.anchor: هر خيالي كوكند دردل وطن رز محشر صورتي خواهد شدن

BURSEVI:v6p235/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p235/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p235/r1.claim: Moses turned away and went back.

BURSEVI:v6p235/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p235/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p235/r2.anchor: {مدبرا} (در حالتي كه كريزان بود از خوف).

BURSEVI:v6p235/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p235/r3.speaker: كشف الأسرار
BURSEVI:v6p235/r3.claim: Kashf al-asrār says Moses turned away and put the serpent behind his back.
BURSEVI:v6p235/r3.anchor: قال في "كشف الأسرار" : أدبر عنها وجعلها تلي ظهره.

BURSEVI:v6p235/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p235/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p235/r4.claim: He did not turn back or retrace his steps; the word is also used of a combatant returning to the charge after fleeing.
BURSEVI:v6p235/r4.anchor: ولم يرجع على عقبه من عقب المقاتل إذا كر بعد الفر

BURSEVI:v6p235/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p235/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p235/r5.claim: Moses was frightened because he thought the event meant his own death, as the reassurance that follows indicates.
BURSEVI:v6p235/r5.anchor: وإنما اعتراه الرعب لظنه أن ذلك الأمر أريد به هلاك نفسه ويدل عليه قوله : يا موسى}

BURSEVI:v6p235/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p235/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p235/r6.claim: The command means fear no one besides God, trusting Him; it may also mean fear nothing at all.
BURSEVI:v6p235/r6.anchor: أي : من غيري ثقة بي أو مطلقا لقوله : {إني لا يخاف لدى} عندي {المرسلون}

BURSEVI:v6p235/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p235/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p235/r7.claim: Messengers are free of fear while receiving revelation, absorbed in witnessing God; at other times they fear God most or fear a bad outcome from Him.
BURSEVI:v6p235/r7.anchor: فإنه يدل على نفي الخوف عنهم مطلقا لكن لا في جميع الأوقات بل حين يوحى إليهم بوقت الخطاب

BURSEVI:v6p235/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p235/r8.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v6p235/r8.claim: Whoever flees to God from all else is secured from all else; illuminated hearts receiving gifts are told not to fear because they are with God.
BURSEVI:v6p235/r8.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : يعني من فر إلى الله عما سواه يؤمنه الله مما سواه ويقول له : لا تخف فإنك لدي

BURSEVI:v6p235/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p235/r9.speaker: عرائس البيان
BURSEVI:v6p235/r9.claim: The serpent is a manifestation of divine majesty; messengers do not fear witnessing that majesty because they know the secrets of lordship.
BURSEVI:v6p235/r9.anchor: وفي "عرائس البيان" : لا تخف من الثعبان فإن ما ترى ظهور تجلي عظمتي ولا يخاف من مشاهدة عظمتي

BURSEVI:v6p235/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p235/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p235/r10.claim: The reassurance also alludes to Moses’ lingering fear over having killed the Copt.
BURSEVI:v6p235/r10.anchor: ولما علم أن موسى كان مستشعرا حقيقة من قتله القبطي قال تعريضا به :

STUDYQURAN:27:10/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:27:10/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:27:10/r1.claim: The opening of verse 10 can connect to verse 9, yielding the sense: God the Mighty, the Wise therefore commands Moses to cast his staff.
STUDYQURAN:27:10/r1.anchor: And at the start of v. 10 could also be understood as connecting v. 10 to the statement in v. 9

STUDYQURAN:27:10/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:27:10/r2.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:27:10/r2.claim: Without returning can mean without looking to either side, indicating that Moses hesitated so little he did not glance sideways.
STUDYQURAN:27:10/r2.anchor: Without returning is also interpreted to mean without looking to one side or the other

TAB-FULL:v18p14#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p14#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p14#2/r1.claim: Jānn is a known kind of snake, and the serpent looked like a large one of that kind.
TAB-FULL:v18p14#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن جريج: " {وألق عصاك فلما رآها تهتز كأنها جان} [النمل: 10] قال: حين تحولت حية تسعى

TAB-FULL:v18p14#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p14#2/r2.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v18p14#2/r2.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the staff had transformed into a serpent that moved along.
TAB-FULL:v18p14#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن جريج: " {وألق عصاك فلما رآها تهتز كأنها جان} [النمل: 10] قال: حين تحولت حية تسعى

TAB-FULL:v18p14#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p14#2/r3.speaker: الراجز
TAB-FULL:v18p14#2/r3.claim: An anonymous rajaz poet's use of jinnān for snakes supports the lexical sense of jānn as a kind of snake.
TAB-FULL:v18p14#2/r3.anchor: أعناق جنان وهاما رجفا وعنقا بعد الرسيم خيطفا

TAB-FULL:v18p14#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p14#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p14#2/r4.claim: Moses turned away and fled because he was afraid of the serpent.

TAB-FULL:v18p14#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p14#2/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p14#2/r5.claim: Lam yuʿaqqib means that he did not return; ʿaqiba is used of going back on one's tracks to where one began.
TAB-FULL:v18p14#2/r5.anchor: {ولم يعقب} [النمل: 10] يقول: ولم يرجع؛ من قولهم: عقب فلان: إذا رجع على عقبه إلى حيث بدأ.

TAB-FULL:v18p14#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p14#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v18p14#2/r6.claim: Mujāhid glosses the phrase as not returning.
TAB-FULL:v18p14#2/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قول الله: " {ولم يعقب} [النمل: 10] قال: لم يرجع

TAB-FULL:v18p14#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p14#2/r7.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v18p14#2/r7.claim: Qatādah glosses it as not looking back.

TAB-FULL:v18p14#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p14#2/r8.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v18p14#2/r8.claim: Ibn Zayd recounts Moses' fear after the staff became a serpent: he kept fleeing despite reassurance, turned only after God restored it to a staff, then returned and later wielded it confidently against Pharaoh.
TAB-FULL:v18p14#2/r8.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: " {ولم يعقب} [النمل: 10] قال: لم يرجع، {يا موسى} [النمل: 9] قال: لما ألقى العصا صارت حية، فرعب منها وجزع، فقال الله:

TABATABAI:27:8-10/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:27:8-10/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:27:8-10/r10.claim: Ihtizāz is vigorous movement; a jann is a small, swift snake; idbār is turning away, and lam yuʿaqqib means not turning back after flight.
TABATABAI:27:8-10/r10.anchor: الاهتزاز التحرك الشديد، والجان الحية الصغيرة السريعة الحركة، والإدبار خلاف الإقبال

TABATABAI:27:8-10/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:27:8-10/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:27:8-10/r11.claim: The explanatory fa in “when he saw it” marks an omitted sequence: after Moses threw the staff, it became a manifest serpent and moved like a jann before he fled.
TABATABAI:27:8-10/r11.anchor: وفي الآية حذف وإيجاز تفصح عنه الفاء الفصيحة في قوله { فلما رآها تهتز }

TABATABAI:27:8-10/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:27:8-10/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:27:8-10/r12.claim: There is no conflict with accounts calling it a great serpent: the comparison concerns the speed and agitation of its motion, not its size or identity.
TABATABAI:27:8-10/r12.anchor: فإن التشبيه إنما وقع في الاهتزاز وسرعة الحركة والاضطراب حيث شاهد العصا وقد تبدلت ثعبانا عظيم الجثة

TABATABAI:27:8-10/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:27:8-10/r13.speaker: قول غير مسمى
TABATABAI:27:8-10/r13.claim: Another view says the staff first appeared as a jann in Ṭā Hā and later as a manifest serpent before Pharaoh in al-Aʿrāf and al-Shuʿarāʾ; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says this does not resolve the comparison problem.
TABATABAI:27:8-10/r13.anchor: وقيل إن آية العصا كانت مختلفة الظهور فقد ظهرت العصا لأول مرة في صورة الجان كما وقع في سورة طه

TABATABAI:27:10-11/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:27:10-11/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:27:10-11/r1.claim: “Do not fear” is a general assurance against anything harmful while Moses is in God's presence; “with Me” makes divine proximity a state of safety, echoed by the al-Qasas wording.
TABATABAI:27:10-11/r1.anchor: فإن تقييد النفي بقوله { لدي } يفيد أن مقام القرب والحضور يلازم الأمن ولا يجامع مكروها

TABATABAI:27:10-11/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:27:10-11/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:27:10-11/r2.claim: Moses fled from an overwhelming danger he could not repel, unarmed except for the staff that had become frightening; no prior instruction forbade flight, so his response was not blameworthy cowardice.
TABATABAI:27:10-11/r2.anchor: وقد كان أعزل لا سلاح معه إلا عصاه وهي التي يخافها على نفسه ولم يرد عليه من جانبه تعالى أمر سابق

TABATABAI:27:10-11/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:27:10-11/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:27:10-11/r3.claim: Messengers' safety in God's presence is bestowed through divine instruction and discipline, not an innate immunity; the first revelation to Moses teaches and trains him rather than rebuking him.
TABATABAI:27:10-11/r3.anchor: فهم لا يملكون هذه الكرامة من عند أنفسهم بل إنما ذلك بتعليم من الله وتأديب

TABRISI:27:8-10/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:8-10/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:27:8-10/r7.claim: The text omits that Moses cast the staff and it turned into a serpent.
TABRISI:27:8-10/r7.anchor: وفي الكلام حذف تقديره فألقاها فصارت حية

TABRISI:27:8-10/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:8-10/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:27:8-10/r8.claim: The staff's serpent moved like a small snake although it was a large dragon; its rapid motion startled Moses.
TABRISI:27:8-10/r8.anchor: أي تتحرك كما يتحرك الجان وهو الحية التي ليست بعظيمة وإنما شبهها بالجان في خفة حركتها

TABRISI:27:8-10/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:8-10/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:27:8-10/r9.claim: Another view distinguishes the two forms: it became a dragon when Moses met Pharaoh but a small serpent at the first prophetic encounter.
TABRISI:27:8-10/r9.anchor: وقيل: إن الحالتين مختلفتان لأن الحال التي صارت ثعبانا هي الحال التي لقي فيها فرعون

TABRISI:27:8-10/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:8-10/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:27:8-10/r10.claim: Walla mudbiran means Moses turned and retreated backward.
TABRISI:27:8-10/r10.anchor: أي رجع إلى ورائه { ولم يعقب

TABRISI:27:8-10/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:8-10/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:27:8-10/r11.claim: Lam yuʿaqqib means he did not return; commentators say he neither looked back nor stopped.
TABRISI:27:8-10/r11.anchor: أي لم يرجع ولم راجع معقب والمفسرون يقولون لم يلتفت ولم يقف

TABRISI:27:8-10/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:8-10/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:27:8-10/r12.claim: God reassures Moses that a messenger does not commit grave wrong or neglect an obligation that would give reason to fear divine punishment.
TABRISI:27:8-10/r12.anchor: وهذا تسكين من الله سبحانه لموسى ونهي له عن الخوف يقول له إنك مرسل والمرسل لا يخاف لأنه

THALABI:v7p190/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p190/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p190/r6.claim: Tahtazzu means that the staff moved; jān here is a quick, small-bodied snake.
THALABI:v7p190/r6.anchor: فلما رآها تهتز تتحرك كأنها جان وهي الحية الخفيفة الصغيرة الجسم

THALABI:v7p190/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p190/r7.speaker: الكلبي
THALABI:v7p190/r7.claim: Al-Kalbi says the snake was neither small nor large.
THALABI:v7p190/r7.anchor: وقال الكلبي: لا صغيرة ولا كبيرة.

THALABI:v7p190/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p190/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p190/r8.claim: One reconciliation is that the staff first became a jān and later a great thuʿbān, swelling from staff-size into a huge snake.
THALABI:v7p190/r8.anchor: أنها في أول أمرها جان وفي آخر الأمر ثعبان

THALABI:v7p190/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p190/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p190/r9.claim: Another reconciliation is that the snake was swift and light like a jān, while having a thuʿbān's shape and strength.
THALABI:v7p190/r9.anchor: أنها في سرعة الجان وخفته وفي صورة الثعبان وقوته

THALABI:v7p190/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p190/r10.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v7p190/r10.claim: Qatada explains that Moses did not look back.
THALABI:v7p190/r10.anchor: ولم يرجع، قال قتادة: ولم يلتفت.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p170/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p170/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p170/r1.claim: The verse omits that Moses threw the staff and it became a moving snake because those details are stated in al-Araf and al-Shuara.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p170/r1.anchor: في الآية محذوف؛ تقديره: فألقاها فصارت حية تهتز {فلما رآها تهتز كأنها جان} وحذف فألقاها؛ لأنه ذكر في سورتين؛ الأعراف، والشعراء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p170/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p170/r2.speaker: الليث وابن شميل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p170/r2.claim: Al-Layth defines a jaan as a white snake; Ibn Shumayl describes it as small, smooth, harmless, and says its plural is jinan.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p170/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p170/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p170/r3.claim: A hadith prohibits killing the white, harmless snakes found in houses, called the house jinan.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p170/r3.anchor: وفي الحديث: نهى عن قتل جنان البيوت؛ وهي حيات بيض تكون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p170/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p170/r4.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p170/r4.claim: Abu Ishaq says the staff moved with a jaan’s quick, light motion while retaining the form of a great serpent.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p170/r4.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: المعنى: أن العصا صارت تتحرك كما يتحرك الجان حركة خفيفة وكانت في صورة ثعبان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p170/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p170/r5.speaker: ثعلب
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p170/r5.claim: Thaʿlab says the comparison describes the snake’s size as a serpent’s and its speed as a jaan’s, explaining the two descriptions elsewhere.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p170/r5.anchor: شبهها في عظمها بالثعبان، وفي خفتها بالجان، فلذلك قال الله تعالى مرة: {كأنها جان} ومرة: {فإذا هي ثعبان مبين}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p170/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p170/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p170/r6.claim: Another view treats the descriptions as successive stages: it is first a jaan, then grows until it becomes a huge serpent.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p170/r6.anchor: وقيل: الاختلاف في التشبيه لاختلاف الحالين؛ فالجان عبارة عن أول حالها ثم لا تزال تزيد وتربو حتى تصير ثعبانا عظيما

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p171/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p171/r1.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p171/r1.claim: Moses fled from fear of the snake and did not return.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p171/r1.anchor: قال مقاتل: من الخوف من الحية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p171/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p171/r2.speaker: مجاهد وأهل اللغة وشمر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p171/r2.claim: The word means returning after turning away to fight; Shammar says every person who returns is called a muʿaqqib.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p171/r2.anchor: يقال: عقب فلان إذا رجع يقاتل بعد أن ولى (¬2). وهذا قول مجاهد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p171/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p171/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p171/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the phrase as meaning that Moses did not stop.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p171/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: {ولم يعقب} لم يقف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p171/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p171/r4.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p171/r4.claim: Qatada explains it as meaning that Moses did not look back; al-Wahidi says these are glosses rather than full exegesis.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p171/r4.anchor: وقال قتادة: لم يلتفت (¬7). وهذان معنى، وليس بتفسير

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p171/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p171/r5.speaker: سفيان
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p171/r5.claim: Sufyan’s reported Arabic gloss is that Moses did not remain or linger.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p171/r5.anchor: وروى شمر عن عبد الصمد عن سفيان: لم يمكث، قال: وهو من كلام العرب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p171/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p171/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p171/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says messengers whom God has sent with His message need not fear in God’s presence.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p171/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس: لا # يخاف عندي من أرسلته برسالتي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p171/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p171/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p171/r7.claim: God does not frighten prophets once He grants them safety; Moses should not fear the snake, since a messenger secured from divine punishment has no reason to fear it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p171/r7.anchor: والمعنى: لا يخيف الله الأنبياء، أي: إذا أمنهم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:10-14/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:10-14/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:10-14/r2.claim: It resembles a quick, light snake.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:10-14/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:10-14/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:10-14/r3.claim: Moses ran away and neither returned nor looked back.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:10-14/r3.anchor: ولى مدبرا ولم يعقب } ولم يرجع ولم يلتفت

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:10-14/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:10-14/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:10-14/r4.claim: The exception concerns one who wronged himself but then repented.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:10-14/r4.anchor: إلا من ظلم } لكن من ظلم نفسه { ثم بدل حسنا بعد سوء } أي: تاب

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:10-14/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:10-14/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:10-14/r5.claim: God is forgiving and merciful to the repentant person.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:10-14/r5.anchor: ثم بدل حسنا بعد سوء } أي: تاب { فإني غفور رحيم

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p534#2/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p534#2/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p534#2/r1.claim: The staff seemed like a snake, as the parallel account says it became a serpent moving swiftly.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p534#2/r1.anchor: {فلما رآها تهتز كأنها جان} [النمل: 10] كأنها حية، وقال في آية أخرى: {فإذا هي حية تسعى} [طه: 20] .

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p534#2/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p534#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p534#2/r3.claim: Qatāda explains “did not turn back” as not looking back.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p534#2/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p534#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p534#2/r4.claim: Mujāhid explains the phrase as not returning.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p534#2/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p534#2/r6.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p534#2/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan says messengers are secure with God in this life and the next as people of divine friendship and love; Moses, who killed the Egyptian, repented and was forgiven.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p534#2/r6.anchor: تفسير الحسن: {لا يخاف لدي المرسلون} [النمل: 10] في الآخرة وفي الدنيا، لأنهم أهل الولاية وأهل المحبة:

QASHANI:27:9-10/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:27:9-10/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:27:9-10/r2.claim: Moses's staff is his sanctified self, joined to the light of holiness; after spiritual discipline he should release it and not prevent its movement, since it has become illumined.
QASHANI:27:9-10/r2.anchor: عصا نفسك القدسية المؤتلفة بشعاع القدس

QASHANI:27:9-10/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:27:9-10/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:27:9-10/r3.claim: The staff's shaking is the self's movement and renewed life, appearing as an overpowering serpent.
QASHANI:27:9-10/r3.anchor: { فلما رآها } تضطرب وتتحرك { كأنها } حية غالبة بالظهور

QASHANI:27:9-10/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:27:9-10/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:27:9-10/r4.claim: Moses turns toward God, fearing the self's appearance, and does not return but remains occupied with tending what remains.
QASHANI:27:9-10/r4.anchor: لم يرجع وبقي مشتغلا بتدارك البقية

QASHANI:27:9-10/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:27:9-10/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:27:9-10/r5.claim: A self revived after death through will and discipline becomes a veil and trial if it acts independently; Moses need not fear its domination in that case.
QASHANI:27:9-10/r5.anchor: فإن النفس إذا حييت بعد موتها بالإرادة وفنائها بالرياضة إن استقلت بنفسها

QASHANI:27:9-10/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:27:9-10/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:27:9-10/r6.claim: When the self moves by God's command, enlivened by the spirit and divine love rather than its own desire, it is no veil.
QASHANI:27:9-10/r6.anchor: وإذا تحركت بأمري حية بنور الروح والمحبة الحقانية لا بهواها لم تكن حجابا

QASHANI:27:9-10/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:27:9-10/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:27:9-10/r7.claim: God's messengers are those granted subsistence after annihilation and enlivened by His life.
QASHANI:27:9-10/r7.anchor: الذين أرسلتهم بالبقاء بعد الفناء وأحييت نفوسهم بحياتي

ELMALILI:27:9-11/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:27:9-11/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:27:9-11/r2.claim: Moses is told to cast down his staff; at this station he should not rely on anything else.
ELMALILI:27:9-11/r2.anchor: hem asânı bırak yani bu makamda bulunan başka[^1] bir şeye dayanmamalıdır.

ELMALILI:27:9-11/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:27:9-11/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:27:9-11/r3.claim: With a doubled nūn, jān means a light, swift serpent.

ELMALILI:27:9-11/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:27:9-11/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:27:9-11/r4.claim: When Moses sees the staff moving like a swift serpent, he turns and flees without looking back.
ELMALILI:27:9-11/r4.anchor: bırakınca o asâyı sanki çevik bir yılanmış gibi çalkanıyor gördü, görünce

ELMALILI:27:9-11/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:27:9-11/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:27:9-11/r5.claim: God reassures Moses that messengers do not fear while in the divine presence receiving revelation and instruction; their spirits are absorbed in the spiritual realm and receiving commands.
ELMALILI:27:9-11/r5.anchor: Peygamberlere böyle vahyolundukları sırada korkmak yaraşmaz, rûhları tamamen melekûta müncezib ve huzûr-ı izzette evâmir telâkkīsine müstağrak olurlar

ELMALILI:27:9-11/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:27:9-11/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:27:9-11/r6.claim: Though prophets are the greatest scholars and fear God most, they fear nothing besides God; in the station of direct presence, fear of everything else vanishes and only the joy of meeting remains.
ELMALILI:27:9-11/r6.anchor: Fakat Allah’tan başka hiçbir şeyden korkmayacakları gibi, huzurda bulundukları mertebe-i cem‘de bütün hiss-i havf dahi mâsivâ gibi silinip yalnız zevk-i likā kalır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:27:7/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:27:7/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:27:7/r8.claim: Moses was supported by nine miracles; this passage mentions only the staff becoming a serpent and his hand emerging white but unharmed, while other miracles appear elsewhere.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:27:7/r8.anchor: İlâhî mesajı Firavun’a tebliğ etmekle görevlendirilen Hz. Mûsâ dokuz mûcize ile desteklenmiştir

QUSHAYRI:v2p410/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p410/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p410/r5.claim: Another verse first has God ask Moses what he holds in his right hand, and Moses answer that it is his staff and describe its uses.
QUSHAYRI:v2p410/r5.anchor: في آية أخرى بين أنه سأله ، وقال له على وجه التقرير

QUSHAYRI:v2p410/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p410/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p410/r6.claim: God told Moses to throw the familiar staff in order to show a great sign that would give him complete certainty.
QUSHAYRI:v2p410/r6.anchor: وذلك لأنه أراد أن يريه فيها من عظيم البرهان ما يجعل له كمال اليقين

QUSHAYRI:v2p410/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p410/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p410/r7.claim: The staff became first a small snake, then a large serpent; Moses fled in fear that God might direct it against him, since he knew God can punish as He wills.
QUSHAYRI:v2p410/r7.anchor: فقلبها الله ثعبانا ، أولا حية صغيرة ثم صارت حية كبيرة ، فأوجس في نفسه موسى خيفة

QUSHAYRI:v2p410/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p410/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p410/r8.claim: The assurance means messengers should not fear; it allows prophets to commit sins outside delivering revelation if they do not persist, while those who deny prophetic sin place Moses' fear before prophethood.
QUSHAYRI:v2p410/r8.anchor: وهذا يدل على جواز الذنب على الأنبياء عليهم السلام فيما لا يتعلق بتبليغ الرسالة بشرط ترك الإصرار

QUSHAYRI:v2p410/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p410/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p410/r9.claim: Moses knew the Real was addressing him when he saw the staff change; God's own informing could establish that knowledge necessarily or through inference, with the staff and white hand as miracles proving His statement.

BURHAN:v1p118/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p118/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p118/r9.claim: Al-Naml begins the command to throw the staff with وألق; al-Qaṣaṣ has وأن ألق.
BURHAN:v1p118/r9.anchor: فى النمل ﴿ وألق عصاك ﴾ وفى القصص

BURHAN:v4p237/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p237/r10.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p237/r10.claim: For “except the one who does wrong,” the majority takes a disconnected exception, while the particle can also function coordinatively as “and.”
BURHAN:v4p237/r10.anchor: وقوله ﴿ إني لا يخاف لدي المرسلون إلا من ظلم ﴾ 4 أي ومن ظلم تاولها الجمهور على الاستثناء المنقطع

BURHAN:v3p349/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p349/r10.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p349/r10.claim: The command to cast down the staff is coordinated with the report 'it was blessed'; its wording is imperative while its sense is reported speech.
BURHAN:v3p349/r10.anchor: فقوله ﴿ وألق ﴾ معطوف على قوله ﴿ أن بورك ﴾ ف ألق وإن كان إنشاء لفظا لكنه خبر معنى

BURHAN:v3p350/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p350/r2.speaker: الفارسي
BURHAN:v3p350/r2.claim: Al-Farisi and Abu al-Baqa allow būrika to be a prayer, not a report; then both coordinated clauses are performative in meaning.
BURHAN:v3p350/r2.anchor: لجواز أن يكون دعاء وهو إنشاء وقد ذكر هذا التقدير الفارسي وأبو البقاء

BURHAN:v2p53/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p53/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p53/r4.claim: Moses' staff was a large serpent in its created form but resembled a small snake in its quick movement, reconciling the descriptions.
BURHAN:v2p53/r4.anchor: وذلك لأن خلقها خلق الثعبان العظيم واهتزازها وحركاتها وخفتها كاهتزاز الجان وخفته

ITQAN:v3p178/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p178/r8.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p178/r8.claim: “He turned away fleeing” is not emphatic because turning can occur without fleeing; the command to turn one’s face toward the Sacred Mosque shows the difference.
ITQAN:v3p178/r8.anchor: وليس منه ﴿ ولى مدبرا ﴾ لأن التولية قد لا تكون إدبارا

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p322#4/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p322#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p322#4/r1.claim: A jān is a snake that is not large.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p322#4/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p322#4/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p322#4/r2.claim: Lam yuʿaqqib means he did not return; another gloss is that he did not look back.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p322#4/r2.anchor: {ولم يعقب} لم يرجع. ويقال: لم يلتفت (3) يقال: كر على القوم وما عقب.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p322#4/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p322#4/r3.speaker: أهل النظر
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p322#4/r3.claim: Some scholars derive yuʿaqqib from ʿaqib, the heel.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p322#4/r3.anchor: ويرى أهل النظر: أنه مأخوذ من "العقب" (4) .

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p322#5/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p322#5/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p322#5/r1.claim: He refers readers to Taʾwīl Mushkil al-Qurʾān for the explanation of this phrase, without restating it here.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p322#5/r1.anchor: {يا موسى لا تخف إني لا يخاف لدي المرسلون * إلا من ظلم} مفسر في كتاب "تأويل المشكل" (5) .

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p139/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p139/r4.speaker: الفراء
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p139/r4.claim: Al-Farra takes the exception as implicit: messengers do not fear, while others do, except a wrongdoer who repents, who need not fear.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p139/r4.anchor: وهذا قول الفراء، وهو يبعد: لأن العرب إنما تحذف من الكلام ما يدل عليه ما يظهر

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p139/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p139/r5.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p139/r5.claim: Ibn Qutayba rejects al-Farra's ellipsis because Arabic omits only what the expressed wording indicates, and this reading lacks such a cue.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p139/r5.anchor: وهذا قول الفراء، وهو يبعد: لأن العرب إنما تحذف من الكلام ما يدل عليه ما يظهر

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p139/r6.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p139/r6.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p139/r6.claim: Moses first fears the serpent, then God reassures him; the exception addresses his further fear over killing a man, which repentance and regret can remove.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p139/r6.anchor: قال أبو محمد: والذي عندي فيه، والله أعلم، أن موسى عليه السلام، لما خاف الثعبان وولى ولم يعقب

NAHHAS:v3p199/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p199/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p199/r1.claim: The phrase كأنها جان is circumstantial; جان means a large serpent in Arab usage.
NAHHAS:v3p199/r1.anchor: والجان عند العرب الثعبان وهو الحية العظيمة

NAHHAS:v3p199/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p199/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p199/r2.anchor: ولى مدبرا ) على الحال ( ولم يعقب ) قال قتادة

NAHHAS:v3p199/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p199/r3.speaker: قتادة
NAHHAS:v3p199/r3.claim: Qatada explains لم يعقب as meaning that Moses did not turn around.

NAHHAS:v3p199/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p199/r4.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p199/r4.claim: Moses is told not to fear the snake and its harm.
NAHHAS:v3p199/r4.anchor: أي قيل له لا تخف من الحية وضررها

NAHHAS:v3p199/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p199/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p199/r5.claim: This completes God's statement to Moses.
NAHHAS:v3p199/r5.anchor: ( إني لا يخاف لدي المرسلون ) هذا تمام الكلام

SAMIN-DURR:27:10/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:10/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:27:10/r1.claim: Wa-alqi is coordinated with the preceding nominal declarative sentence; Sībawayh does not require coordinated sentences to share grammatical form.
SAMIN-DURR:27:10/r1.anchor: عطف على ما قبله من الجملة الاسمية الخبرية. وقد تقدم أن سيبويه لا يشترط تناسب الجمل

SAMIN-DURR:27:10/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:10/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:27:10/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī coordinates alqi with bӯrika, supplying “and it was said to him: throw your staff,” and supports it with the repeated explanatory an in the narrative.
SAMIN-DURR:27:10/r2.anchor: لأن المعنى: نودي أن بورك. وقيل له: ألق عصاك

SAMIN-DURR:27:10/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:10/r3.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:27:10/r3.claim: The Shaykh objects that al-Zamakhsharī’s cited innahu is itself coordinated with bӯrika, not the quoted command; the paraphrase requires an extra “it was said to him.”
SAMIN-DURR:27:10/r3.anchor: قال: الشيخ: " وقوله: " إنه معطوف على " بورك "

SAMIN-DURR:27:10/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:10/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:27:10/r4.claim: The author rejects requiring parallel sentence forms for coordination and supports Sībawayh’s allowance of nonparallel clauses.

SAMIN-DURR:27:10#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:10#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:27:10#2/r1.claim: Tahitazzu is circumstantial from the object pronoun in tarāhā, since the seeing is visual.
SAMIN-DURR:27:10#2/r1.anchor: جملة حالية من هاء " تراها " لأن الرؤية بصرية

SAMIN-DURR:27:10#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:10#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:27:10#2/r2.claim: Kaʾannahā jānn may be a second circumstantial clause or a nested circumstantial clause from the pronoun in tahitazzu.
SAMIN-DURR:27:10#2/r2.anchor: يجوز أن تكون حالا ثانية، وأن تكون حالا من ضمير " تهتز "

SAMIN-DURR:27:10#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:10#2/r3.speaker: الحسن والزهري وعمرو بن عبيد
SAMIN-DURR:27:10#2/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan, al-Zuhrī, and ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd read jāʾn with hamza in place of alif.
SAMIN-DURR:27:10#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ الحسن والزهري وعمرو بن عبيد " جأن " بهمزة مكان الألف

SAMIN-DURR:27:10#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:10#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:27:10#2/r4.claim: Wa-lam yuʿaqqib may coordinate with wallā or be another circumstantial clause; it means he did not turn back.
SAMIN-DURR:27:10#2/r4.anchor: يجوز أن يكون عطفا على " ولى " ، وأن يكون حالا أخرى

SAMIN-DURR:27:10#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:10#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:27:10#2/r5.claim: Poetry uses ʿaqqabū for turning back, attesting the sense “did not return on his tracks.”
SAMIN-DURR:27:10#2/r5.anchor: فما عقبوا إذ قيل: هل من معقب

ZAJJAJ:v4p109/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p109/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p109/r1.claim: The serpent moved with a jinn's light, quick motion though it had the shape of a great snake.
ZAJJAJ:v4p109/r1.anchor: تتحرك كما يتحرك الجان حركة خفيفة

ZAJJAJ:v4p109/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p109/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p109/r2.claim: The الثعبان is the great kind of snake.

ZAJJAJ:v4p109/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p109/r3.speaker: التفسير
ZAJJAJ:v4p109/r3.claim: Exegetical reports explain لم يعقب as Moses not looking back.
ZAJJAJ:v4p109/r3.anchor: جاء في التفسير " لم يعقب " لم يلتفت

ZAJJAJ:v4p109/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p109/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p109/r4.claim: Linguists explain it as not returning; عقب can mean returning to fight after retreat.
ZAJJAJ:v4p109/r4.anchor: قد عقب فلان إذا رجع يقاتل بعد أن ولى

ZAJJAJ:v4p109/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p109/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p109/r5.claim: Labid's verse uses المعقب to witness the sense of returning after retreat.
ZAJJAJ:v4p109/r5.anchor: قال لبيد: حتى تهجر في الرواح وهاجه. . . طلب المعقب حقه المظلوم

ZAJJAJ:v4p109/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p109/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p109/r6.claim: لدي means عندي, at My presence.

ASAD-NOTES:27:7#n8/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:27:7#n8/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:27:7#n8/r1.claim: Asad points to 20:17–20 for comparison with this account of Moses.

ASAD-NOTES:27:7#n9/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:27:7#n9/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:27:7#n9/r1.claim: Asad points to note 14 on 20:20–21 for a tentative explanation of the symbolism of the staff miracle.
ASAD-NOTES:27:7#n9/r1.anchor: For a tentative explanation of the symbolism underlying the miracle of the staff, see note 14 on 20:2O~2l.

ASAD-NOTES:27:9#n10/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:27:9#n10/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:27:9#n10/r1.claim: Asad renders illa here as "and neither" and points to his explanation at 4:29.
ASAD-NOTES:27:9#n10/r1.anchor: For my rendering of illa, in this context, as "and neither", see note 38 on 4:29.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#2/r7.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#2/r7.claim: The end of al-Naml echoes its opening: Moses recoils in fear at the moving staff, and the sura later speaks of terror at the Resurrection.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#2/r7.anchor: ثم انظر مرة أخرى كيف ناسب ختام السورة أولها وما ورد فيها من فزع في قصة موسى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p108/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p108/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p108/r2.claim: Al-Naml’s direct imperative reports God’s exact words and signals honor; al-Qaṣaṣ’s أن ألق describes the meaning of the call without requiring those exact words.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p108/r2.anchor: فقوله: {وَأَلْقِ عَصَاكَ} قولٌ مباشر من رب العزة، وهو دال على التكريم

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p91/r10.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p91/r10.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p91/r10.claim: Naml gives the command to throw the staff directly; al-Qaṣaṣ prefixes it with wa-an.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p91/r11.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p91/r11.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p91/r11.claim: Al-Qaṣaṣ adds a command to come forward before saying not to fear; Naml has only the shorter reassurance.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p91/r12.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p91/r12.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p91/r12.claim: Naml says messengers do not fear in God's presence; al-Qaṣaṣ directly assures Musa that he is among the safe.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p91/r12.anchor: {إِنِّي لاَ يَخَافُ لَدَيَّ المرسلون} {إِنَّكَ مِنَ الآمنين}

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p91/r13.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p91/r13.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p91/r13.claim: Naml adds an exception for one who sinned and then replaced evil with good; the author lists no parallel exception in al-Qaṣaṣ.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p91/r13.anchor: {إِلاَّ مَن ظَلَمَ} {وَأَدْخِلْ يَدَكَ فِي جَيْبِكَ} {اسلك يَدَكَ}

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p109/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p109/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p109/r1.claim: Al-Qaṣaṣ adds aqbil because its detailed telling allows fuller speech and Musa's pervasive fear suggests he fled farther, so he must be called back as well as reassured.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p109/r1.anchor: مقام الإيجاز في النمل يستدعي عدم الإطالة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p109/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p109/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p109/r2.claim: The recurrent atmosphere of fear in al-Qaṣaṣ indicates Musa had fled far, prompting the additional call to come forward.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p109/r2.anchor: أن شيوع جو الخوف في القصص يدل على إيغال موسى في الهرب، فدعاه إلى الإقبال وعدم الخوف

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p109/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p109/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p109/r3.claim: Al-Qaṣaṣ assures a frightened Musa that he is safe; Naml's statement about messengers not fearing in God's presence honors him by hinting he belongs among them.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p109/r3.anchor: ذلك أن المقام في سورة القصص مقام الخوف

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p109/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p109/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p109/r4.claim: Naml's ladayya suggests closeness; its direct ya-Musa and alqi, without explanatory particles, likewise signal proximity between God and Musa.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p109/r4.anchor: ثم انظر كيف قال: {لَدَيَّ} مُشْعِراً بالقُربِ وهو زيادةٌ في التكريم والتشريف

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p110/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p110/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p110/r1.claim: Lā yakhāfu ladayya means messengers feel no fear in God's presence, not that they fear nothing of Him; the Prophet's statement that he is most God-fearing supports their reverence.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p110/r1.anchor: لأن المرسلين لا يخافون بحضرته، ولكنهم يخشونه ويخافونه كل الخوف

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p110/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p110/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p110/r2.claim: Naml's exception for a wrongdoer who reforms is omitted in al-Qaṣaṣ because qualifying the direct assurance that Musa is among the safe would sound incoherent.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p110/r2.anchor: لأنه لا يحسن أن يقال: (إنك من الآمنين إلا من ظلم، ثم بدل حسناً بعد سوء..) ولو قال هذا لم يكن كلاماً

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p110/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p110/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p110/r3.claim: The reform exception fits the Queen of Sheba, who left sun-worship and submitted to God; Moses was already a believer, and his confession of wrong concerned killing the Egyptian, not a change from disbelief.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p110/r3.anchor: فإنها ظلمت نفسها بكفرها وسجودِها للشمس من دون الله، ثم بدّلت حُسْناً بعد سوء، فأسلمتْ لله رب العالمين

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p92/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p92/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p92/r5.claim: Fear frames al-Qaṣaṣ from Musa's mother's alarm to Musa's fear after killing the Egyptian and his fearful flight from the city, while Naml mentions fear only at the staff miracle.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p92/r5.anchor: في سورة القصص، كان جو القصة مطبوعاً بطابع الخوف الذي يسيطر على موسى، عليه السلام

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p93/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p93/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p93/r1.claim: Fear continues in al-Qaṣaṣ as Musa prays for rescue, receives reassurance in Midian, fears Pharaoh's killing and denial, and asks Aaron to assist him; this contrasts with Naml's brief, less fearful story.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p93/r1.anchor: وهذا الطابع - أعني طابع الخوف - يبقى ملازماً للقصة إلى أواخرها

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p72/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p72/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p72/r1.claim: Fear persists through the Qasas account, including Moses’ fear of being killed or rejected, while Naml mentions fear only when he sees the staff; this difference shapes the wording.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p72/r1.anchor: وهذا الطابع ـ أعني طابع الخوف ـ يبقى ملازما للقصة إلى أواخرها، بل حتى إنه لما كلفه ربه بالذهاب إلى فرعون راجعه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p87/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p87/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p87/r2.claim: The direct command “Throw your staff” in Naml is a direct divine utterance and marks honor; the أن construction in Qasas reports the meaning of the call, not necessarily its exact words.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p87/r2.anchor: فقوله: "وأَلْقِ عَصاك" قول مباشر من رب العزة، وهو دال على التكريم

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p87/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p87/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p87/r3.claim: Qasas adds أقبل because its fuller narrative and pervasive atmosphere of fear call Moses to approach as well as to stop fearing; Naml's concise context omits it.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p87/r3.anchor: منها: أن مقام الإيجاز في النمل يستدعي عدم الإطالة بخلاف مقام التفصيل في القصص.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p87/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p87/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p87/r4.claim: Qasas is a scene of fear, so Moses is reassured that he is among the safe; Naml instead gives the general assurance that messengers do not fear in God's presence.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p87/r4.anchor: ذلك أن المقام في سورة القصص مقام الخوف، والخائف يحتاج إلى الأمن فأمنه قائلا: "إنّكَ مِنَ الآمِنينَ"

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p88/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p88/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p88/r1.claim: Saying messengers do not fear in God’s presence indirectly identifies Musa as one of them, honoring him.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p88/r1.anchor: فألمح بذلك إلى نه منهم، وهذا تكريم وتشريف

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p88/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p88/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p88/r2.claim: Ladayya suggests nearness, which adds to the honor and distinction.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p88/r2.anchor: مشعرا بالقرب، وهو زيادة في التكريم والتشريف

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p88/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p88/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p88/r3.claim: The direct ‘ya Musa’ and ‘wa-alqi asaka’ omit Qasas’s an, signaling nearness in both the summons and command.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p88/r3.anchor: فناداه من قرب وأمره من قرب

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p88/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p88/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p88/r4.claim: Messengers are secure in God’s presence while still fearing and revering Him greatly; the verse does not say they do not fear God.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p88/r4.anchor: لأن المرسلين لا يخافون بحضرته، ولكنهم يخشونه ويخافونه كل الخوف

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p88/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p88/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p88/r5.claim: The Prophet’s statement ‘I am the most God-fearing of you’ supports the distinction between security in God’s presence and fear of Him.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p88/r5.anchor: وقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم: (أنا أخشاكم لله)

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p88/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p88/r6.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p88/r6.claim: Naml omits ‘except one who did wrong, then changed to good’ because that exception would make the assurance ‘you are among the secure’ incoherent.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p88/r6.anchor: لا يحسن أن يقال: (إنك من الآمنين إلا من ظلم ثم بدل حسنا بعد سوء)

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p88/r7.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p88/r7.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p88/r7.claim: The queen’s confession of wrongdoing and submission with Solomon exemplifies changing from evil to good, so the exception and forgiveness fit Naml’s context.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p88/r7.anchor: رب إني ظلمت نفسي وأسلمت مع سليمان لله رب العالمين

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p88/r8.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p88/r8.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p88/r8.claim: He anticipates an apparent counterexample: Qasas also says Musa confessed his wrongdoing and God forgave him (28:16).
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p88/r8.anchor: وقد تقول: لقد ورد مثل هذا التعبير في سورة القصص أيضا وهو قوله تعالى:

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1005/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1005/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1005/r1.claim: Jann conveys quick motion and fear: it frightens people, and the serpent-like staff’s rapid movement suits the frightened scene.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1005/r1.anchor: الجان دلالة الحركة السريعة، عصاه تهتز بسرعة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1005/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1005/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1005/r2.claim: The name jann is linked to concealment, in contrast to humans’ visibility.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1005/r2.anchor: وسمي جان لأنه يستتر بمقابل الإنس (الإنس للظهور والجن للستر)

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1005/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1005/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1005/r3.claim: Although jinn are hidden, they can appear in forms; he cites the event involving Abu Hurayra to explain how one could see such a form.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1005/r3.anchor: قد يظهر الجان بشكل أو يتشكل بشكل كما حدث مع أبو هريرة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1005/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1005/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1005/r4.claim: Taha calls the staff a hayya to display God’s power and does not say Musa fled or panicked there.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1005/r4.anchor: الحية جاءت في مكان واحد لبيان قدرة الله تعالى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1005/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1005/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1005/r5.claim: Jann is chosen for Musa’s fear; thubaan is used before Pharaoh because one jann would not impress a crowd of hundreds and the scene calls for size and strength.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1005/r5.anchor: لأنه مع الملأ الموجودين إذا كانوا مئات وتأتي بجان واحد ماذا يؤثر

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1005/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1005/r6.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1005/r6.claim: The account uses thubaan twice before Pharaoh and jann twice with Musa, matching each term to its setting.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1005/r6.anchor: ذكر ثعبان مرتين أمام فرعون وجان مرتين أمام موسى

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p468/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p468/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p468/r1.claim: The preceding verses prepare Moses mentally and emotionally for his mission; the following material gives signs essential for confronting Pharaoh.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p468/r1.anchor: The previous verses guide Moses (sws) regarding the mental and emotional preparation for the mission at hand.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p468/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p468/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p468/r2.claim: The staff is the most important sign and the source from which the remaining signs emanated.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p468/r2.anchor: The most important of these signs was that of the staff from which the rest of the signs emanated.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p468/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p468/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p468/r3.claim: Moses’ flight highlights how initially unfamiliar and strange prophetic experiences frighten a prophet, whom God gradually familiarizes with them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p468/r3.anchor: when it started to swivel like a snake, he got so frightened that he ran away without even looking back.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p468/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p468/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p468/r4.claim: Prophethood is bestowed unexpectedly, not won by desire or demand; prophets accept its obligatory responsibility anxiously after becoming convinced of their divine appointment.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p468/r4.anchor: their desire or demand. In fact, it is bestowed upon them without their expectation

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p468/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p468/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p468/r5.claim: God reassures Moses that he is safe in divine company, while those who reject the messengers face danger.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p468/r5.anchor: in the company of God, His messengers have nothing to fear; they are absolutely safe and secure

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p468/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p468/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p468/r6.claim: Moses is God’s messenger and his staff is a sword, so his enemies should fear him rather than he fear them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p468/r6.anchor: So, why should he fear them; it is they who should fear him.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p377/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p377/r2.speaker: أبو بكر عن عاصم وحفص عن عاصم
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p377/r2.claim: Abu Bakr's transmission from Asim has kasra on the ر and hamza of رآها; Hafs has fatḥa on both.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p377/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p377/r3.speaker: أبو عمرو والكسائي وحمزة وابن عامر وابن كثير ونافع
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p377/r3.claim: Abu Amr has fatḥa on ر and kasra on hamza throughout; al-Kisai and Hamza match Abu Bakr, while Ibn Amir, Ibn Kathir, and Nafi have both fatḥa.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p377/r3.anchor: وفتح أبو عمرو الراء وكسر الهمزة في كل القرآن، والكسائي مثل عاصم في رواية أبي بكر يكسرها وحمزة مثله، ابن عامر يفتح

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p377/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p377/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p377/r4.claim: Al-Farisi notes that the grounds for imala of the two fatḥas were explained earlier.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p377/r4.anchor: قال أبو علي: قد تقدم ذكر وجه إمالة الفتحتين منهما في غير موضع.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p79#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p79#3/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p79#3/r1.claim: Qatāda explains “he did not turn back” as meaning Moses did not look back.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p79#3/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ ولم يعقب ﴾ قال لم يلتفت

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالسواكنإذاوقعبعد.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالسواكنإذاوقعبعد.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالسواكنإذاوقعبعد.claim: Before a following consonant, final alif, yā preceded by kasra, and wāw preceded by ḍamma may be deleted; speakers avoid shifting alif to the heavier yā or wāw when no ambiguity results.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالسواكنإذاوقعبعد.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالسواكنإذاوقعبعد.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالسواكنإذاوقعبعد.claim: The final alif in feminine forms such as ḥublā and maʿzā may drop before the article if context prevents confusion.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالسواكنإذاوقعبعد.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالسواكنإذاوقعبعد.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالسواكنإذاوقعبعد.claim: They preserve or replace the weak ending in forms such as duals when deletion would confuse two with one or feminine with masculine.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالسواكنإذاوقعبعد.anchor: ومثل ذلك قولهم رمت وقالوا رميا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالسواكنإذاوقعبعد.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالسواكنإذاوقعبعد.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالسواكنإذاوقعبعد.claim: A final yā after kasra is dropped in يرمي and يقضي before a following consonant; opening it would confuse the form with the accusative.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالسواكنإذاوقعبعد.anchor: وأما حذف الياء التي قبلها كسرة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالسواكنإذاوقعبعد.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالسواكنإذاوقعبعد.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالسواكنإذاوقعبعد.claim: A final wāw after ḍamma is likewise dropped in يغزو and يدعو when the following consonant creates no ambiguity.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالسواكنإذاوقعبعد.anchor: وأما حذف الواو التي قبلها حرف مضموم

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالسواكنإذاوقعبعد.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالسواكنإذاوقعبعد.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالسواكنإذاوقعبعد.claim: In اخشوا and رموا, they retain the weak ending because dropping it would confuse number or gender; the preceding vowel is also lighter in these forms.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالسواكنإذاوقعبعد.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالسواكنإذاوقعبعد.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالسواكنإذاوقعبعد.claim: He distinguishes deletion before a following consonant from the weak-letter loss in لم يخف; the yā of يهاب and wāw of يخاف illustrate that separate cause.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالسواكنإذاوقعبعد.anchor: لأنه ليس لاستثقال لما بعدها حذفت

ALUSI-FULL:v19p162#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p162#2/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v19p162#2/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari coordinates “cast your staff” with “blessed,” as part of the call's explanation, supported by the parallel wording in 28:30, where أن introduces Moses' commission.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p162#2/r1.anchor: عطف على بورك منتظم معه في سلك تفسير النداء أو نودي أن بورك وأن ألق عصاك

ALUSI-FULL:v19p162#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p162#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p162#2/r2.claim: An objection says the renewed “O Moses” in 28:30 disproves that parsing; the reply is that it continues the same call, or is parenthetical.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p162#2/r2.anchor: وأورد عليه أن تجديد النداء في قوله تعالى ( ياموسى ) الخ يأباه ورد بأنه ليس بتجديد نداء

ALUSI-FULL:v19p162#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p162#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p162#2/r3.claim: Because بورك is declarative and cast is imperative, some reject direct coordination and posit “he was told” or an omitted command; Alusi allows unlike clauses to coordinate in speech meaning, citing Sibawayh, but says the omitted-command account would favor فألق.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p162#2/r3.anchor: واعترض أيضا بأن بورك اخبار والق إنشاء ولا يعطف الانشاء على الاخبار

ALUSI-FULL:v19p162#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p162#2/r4.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v19p162#2/r4.claim: Abu Hayyan coordinates the imperative with إنه أنا الله العزيز الحكيم, allowing unlike nominal and verbal or declarative and imperative clauses to coordinate, as Sibawayh permits.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p162#2/r4.anchor: واختار أبو حيان كون العطف على جملة ( إنه أنا الله العزيز الحكيم ) ولم يبال باختلاف الجملتين

ALUSI-FULL:v19p162#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p162#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p162#2/r5.claim: The fa is explanatory: it elides the obvious casting and transformation into a snake, conveying how quickly the result occurred.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p162#2/r5.anchor: والفاء في قوله تعالى ( فما رءاها تهتز ( فصيحة تفصح عن جملة قد حذفت ثقة بظهورها

ALUSI-FULL:v19p162#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p162#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p162#2/r6.claim: رآها is visual perception, and تهتز is a circumstantial clause describing the object seen.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p162#2/r6.anchor: وجملة ( تهتز ) في موضع الحال من مفعول رأى فانها بصرية كما أشرنا اليه

ALUSI-FULL:v19p162#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p162#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p162#2/r7.claim: A jann is a small, swiftly moving snake; the simile conveys intense motion and agitation despite the staff's great size, as in the description “a manifest serpent” in 7:107.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p162#2/r7.anchor: والجان الحية الصغيرة السرية الحركة شبهها سبحانه في شدة حركتها واضطرابها مع عظم جثتها بصغار الحيات السريعة الحركة

ALUSI-FULL:v19p162#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p162#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p162#2/r8.claim: The phrase كأنها جان is a second circumstantial clause of the object, or a nested circumstance attached to تهتز.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p162#2/r8.anchor: وقوله تعالى : ( كأنها جان ( في موضع حال أخرى منه أو هو حال من ضمير ( تهتز )

ALUSI-FULL:v19p162#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p162#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p162#2/r9.claim: The description of the staff as a small snake's likeness does not conflict with its being called a manifest serpent elsewhere.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p162#2/r9.anchor: في موضع آخر : ( فاذا هي ثعبان مبين )

ALUSI-FULL:v19p163/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p163/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p163/r1.claim: Another view allows different descriptions of the snake because it passed through different forms.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p163/r1.anchor: وقيل : يجوز أن يكون الاخبار عنها بصفات مختلفة باعتبار تنقلها فيها

ALUSI-FULL:v19p163/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p163/r2.speaker: الحسن والزهري وعمرو بن عبيد
ALUSI-FULL:v19p163/r2.claim: Al-Hasan, al-Zuhri, and Amr ibn Ubayd read جأن with an open hamza to avoid two adjacent quiescent letters, as in دأبة and شأبة.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p163/r2.anchor: وقرأ الحسن والزهري وعمرو بن عبيد ( جأن ) بهمزة مفتوحة هربا من التقاء الساكنين

ALUSI-FULL:v19p163/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p163/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p163/r3.claim: ولى مدبرا means that Moses fled.

ALUSI-FULL:v19p163/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p163/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p163/r4.claim: لم يعقب means that Moses did not turn back, using the expression for a fighter who charges again after retreat.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p163/r4.anchor: أي ولم يرجع على عقبه من عقب المقاتل إذا كر بعد الفرار

ALUSI-FULL:v19p163/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p163/r5.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v19p163/r5.claim: Mujahid transmits that لم يعقب means Moses did not turn back.

ALUSI-FULL:v19p163/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p163/r6.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v19p163/r6.claim: A close interpretation attributed to Qatada is that Moses did not look back; al-Raghib gives this sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p163/r6.anchor: وقريب منه قول قتادة : أي لم يتلفت وهو الذي ذكره الراغب

ALUSI-FULL:v19p163/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p163/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p163/r7.claim: Alusi says Moses fled from fear, either through ordinary human instinct at a terrifying sight or because he thought the snake meant him harm.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p163/r7.anchor: وكان ذلك منه عليه السلام لخوف لحقه قيل : لمقتضى البشرية

ALUSI-FULL:v19p163/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p163/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p163/r8.claim: “Do not fear” can mean fear no creature besides God, relying on Him, or can be an unqualified prohibition; it may simply reassure rather than literally forbid fear, or prohibit the suspicion causing it.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p163/r8.anchor: أي من غيري أي مخلوق كان حية أو غيرها ثقة بي

ALUSI-FULL:v19p163/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p163/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p163/r9.claim: One explanation makes this the reason for the prohibition: messengers should not fear while receiving revelation, being absorbed in divine commands and drawn to the unseen realm; the restriction “in My presence” matters because they fear God greatly at other times.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p163/r9.anchor: تعليل للنهي عن الخوف وهو على ما قيل يؤيد أن الخوف كان للظن المذكور

ALUSI-FULL:v19p163/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p163/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p163/r10.claim: Their fear of God in other circumstances accords with 35:28, which says God's learned servants fear Him most.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p163/r10.anchor: فقد قال تعالى : ( إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء )

ALUSI-FULL:v19p163/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p163/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p163/r11.claim: Another explanation is that Moses must not fear anyone else, or fear absolutely: messengers should fear only their final outcome, and none has a bad outcome with God.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p163/r11.anchor: وقيل : المعنى لاتخف من غيري أو لاتخف مطلقا فان الذي ينبغي أن يخاف منه أمثالك المرسلون

ALUSI-FULL:v19p163#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p163#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p163#2/r1.claim: “Bad outcome” means the afterlife, not worldly death, since some messengers were killed; al-Khafaji glosses لدي as “at My meeting,” while Ibn al-Shaykh says “under My judgment.”
ALUSI-FULL:v19p163#2/r1.anchor: والمراد بسوء العاقبة ما في الآخرة لا ما في الدنيا

ALUSI-FULL:v19p163#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p163#2/r2.speaker: الأشعري
ALUSI-FULL:v19p163#2/r2.claim: A reading in the Shihabiyya marginalia says messengers cannot fear a bad end because God secures them from it, and fear would imply distrust.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p163#2/r2.anchor: مما ذكر أن المرسلين عليهم السلام لايخافون سوء العاقبة لأن الله تعالى آمنهم من ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v19p163#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p163#2/r3.speaker: عائشة
ALUSI-FULL:v19p163#2/r3.claim: Aisha asked why the Prophet often prayed for steadfastness; he replied that nothing secured him while hearts were between God's fingers and He could turn a servant's heart.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p163#2/r3.anchor: فقد روي أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام كان يكثر أن يقول

ALUSI-FULL:v19p163#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p163#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p163#2/r4.claim: The apparent sense of 7:99 also supports the possibility of fearing God's devising.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p163#2/r4.anchor: وظاهر بعض الآيات يقتضي ذلك أيضا مثل قوله تعالى : ( فلا يأمن مكر الله إلا القوم الخاسرون )

ALUSI-FULL:v19p163#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p163#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p163#2/r5.claim: Being promised Paradise does not prevent fear of a bad end: the promised Companions still feared, and a concealed divine condition could coexist with glad tidings without implying distrust.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p163#2/r5.anchor: فقد صح أن المبشرين بالجنة من الصحابة رضي الله تعالى عنهم كانوا يخافون من سوء العاقبة مع علمهم ببشارته تعالى إياهم بالجنة

ALUSI-FULL:v19p163#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p163#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p163#2/r6.claim: Even if security means explicit assurance or protection from disbelief, a hidden condition could remain; angels too are protected from such sin yet still fear.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p163#2/r6.anchor: وإن أريد به ما اقتضاه جعله الله تعالى إياهم معصومين من الكفر ونحوه ورد أن الملائكة عليهم السلام جعلهم الله تعالى معصومين من ذلك أيضا وهم يخافون

ALUSI-FULL:v19p164/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p164/r1.speaker: جبريل وميكائيل
ALUSI-FULL:v19p164/r1.claim: An account says Gabriel and Michael wept when Iblis plotted; God asked why, and they answered that they did not feel safe from His devising, to which God told them to remain so.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p164/r1.anchor: ففي الأثر لما مكر بابليس بكى جبرائيل وميكائيل عليهما السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v19p164/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p164/r2.speaker: الأشاعرة
ALUSI-FULL:v19p164/r2.claim: In Ashari doctrine as stated in al-Mawaqif and its commentary, infallibility is God's not creating a sin in a person; this does not make sin impossible because God is not obliged to refrain from creating it.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p164/r2.anchor: ولعل ذلك لأن العصمة عندنا على ما يقتضيه أصل استناد الأشياء كلها إلى الفاعل المختار ابتداء كما في المواقف

ALUSI-FULL:v19p164/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p164/r3.speaker: الحكماء
ALUSI-FULL:v19p164/r3.claim: Philosophers define infallibility as a disposition that prevents indecency, formed by knowledge of sin's harms and obedience's merits and strengthened by continuing revelation; the disposition can still cease.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p164/r3.anchor: وعند الحكماء بناء على ما ذهبوا إليه من القول بالإيجاب واعتبار استعداد القوابل ملكة تمنع الفجور

ALUSI-FULL:v19p164/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p164/r4.speaker: قوم
ALUSI-FULL:v19p164/r4.claim: Some posit an innate property of the person or body that makes sin impossible and use it to infer security; Alusi says that argument fails.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p164/r4.anchor: نعم قال قوم : العصمة تكون خاصية في نفس الشخص أو في بدنه يمتنع بسببها صدور الذنب عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v19p164/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p164/r5.speaker: الشريف الجرجاني
ALUSI-FULL:v19p164/r5.claim: Al-Jurjani's al-Mawaqif commentary argues that impossible sin earns no praise when avoided and cannot be a commanded, rewarded choice; 18:110 also affirms the prophets' shared humanity, distinguished by revelation.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p164/r5.anchor: ففي المواقف وشرحه أنه يكذب هذا القول أنه لو كان صدور الذنب ممتنعا

ALUSI-FULL:v19p164/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p164/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p164/r6.claim: The humanity argument invokes 18:110: prophets resemble other people in humanity and differ through revelation, so sin is not intrinsically impossible for them.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p164/r6.anchor: وأيضا فقوله تعالى : ( قل إنما أنا بشر مثلكم يوحى إلي ) يدل على مماثلتهم عليهم السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v19p164/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p164/r7.speaker: ابن الهمام
ALUSI-FULL:v19p164/r7.claim: Ibn al-Humam defines infallibility as lack of power to sin plus a created restraint that does not compel; Alusi connects this to Maturidi teaching that infallibility preserves the trial and choice, restraining without forcing obedience.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p164/r7.anchor: وذكر الخفاجي في شرح الشفاء عن ابن الهمام أنه قال في التحرير : العصمة عدم القدرة على المعصية وخلق مانع عنها غير ملجيء

ALUSI-FULL:v19p164/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p164/r8.speaker: ابن حجر
ALUSI-FULL:v19p164/r8.claim: Some scholars' statements that prophets' sin is impossible should be understood as legal impossibility, as Ibn Hajar's commentary on the Hamziyya suggests.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p164/r8.anchor: ولعل ما وقع في كلام بعض الأجلة من استحالة وقوع الذنب منهم عليهم السلام محمول على الاستحالة الشرعية

ALUSI-FULL:v19p164/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p164/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p164/r9.claim: Alusi concludes that revelation and reason indicate prophets and angels fear God's devising: sin is legally impossible but rationally possible, God is not obligated, and a promise may have an undisclosed condition; he rejects restricting their fear to awe alone.
