ALUSI-FULL:v19p164/r9.anchor: فالأنبياء والملائكة كلهم خائفون ومن خشيته سبحانه عز وجل مشفقون

ALUSI-FULL:v19p164/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p164/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p164/r10.claim: God could create necessary knowledge that a possible feared event will never occur, granting complete security; this may happen to the people of Paradise, or some servants on Judgment Day, but Alusi sees no indication it happens in this life.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p164/r10.anchor: نعم قد يقال بإمكان حصول الأمن من المكر وذلك بخلق الله تعالى علما ضروريا في العبد بعدم تحقق ما يخاف منه

ALUSI-FULL:v19p164/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p164/r11.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v19p164/r11.claim: An interpretation transmitted by the Imam says messengers need not fear when ordered to display a miracle, though a messenger may fear in other matters.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p164/r11.anchor: وروى الإمام عن بعضهم أنه قال معنى الآية : إني إذا أمرت المرسلين بإظهار معجز

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p146/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p146/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p146/r1.claim: A jān is a small snake that moves and writhes frequently; the staff shook like one.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p146/r1.anchor: {كأنها جان} وهي الحية الصغيرة التي يكثر اضطرابها،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p146/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p146/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p146/r2.claim: Moses fled in fear and did not turn back; ʿaqiba means to return, and every returner is a muʿaqqib.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p146/r2.anchor: {ولى مدبرا} هرب من الخوف، {ولم يعقب} لم يرجع، يقال: عقب فلان إذا رجع، وكل راجع معقب.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p146/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p146/r3.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p146/r3.claim: Qatada explains lam yuʿaqqib as not looking back.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p146/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p146/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p146/r4.claim: Messengers do not fear once God has secured them, though reverential fear that is part of faith remains; the Prophet said he feared God most.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p146/r4.anchor: أما الخوف الذي هو شرط الإيمان فلا يفارقهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:27:9-10/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:9-10/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:9-10/r3.claim: The command to cast down the staff is coordinated with the earlier blessing announcement; the repeated أن after the address to Moses supports this parsing.
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:9-10/r3.anchor: أي نودي أن بورك من في النار وأن ألق عصاك، ويدل عليه قوله

BAYDAWI-FULL:27:9-10/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:9-10/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:9-10/r4.claim: A jān is a light, swiftly moving serpent.

BAYDAWI-FULL:27:9-10/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:9-10/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:9-10/r5.claim: A reading جأن follows the language of someone who intensifies avoidance of two adjacent sukūns while fleeing.
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:9-10/r5.anchor: وقرىء «جأن» على لغة من جد في الهرب من التقاء الساكنين

BAYDAWI-FULL:27:9-10/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:9-10/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:9-10/r6.claim: He turned and did not come back; عَقَّب is used of a fighter who turns back after fleeing.
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:9-10/r6.anchor: ولم يرجع من عقب المقاتل إذا كر بعد الفرار، وإنما رعب

BAYDAWI-FULL:27:9-10/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:9-10/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:9-10/r7.claim: Moses was terrified because he thought the strange event was directed against him, as the reassurance not to fear indicates.
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:9-10/r7.anchor: وإنما رعب لظنه أن ذلك الأمر أريد به ويدل عليه قوله

BAYDAWI-FULL:27:9-10/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:9-10/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:9-10/r8.claim: The reassurance may mean do not fear anyone besides Me, trusting in Me, or may be unrestricted.
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:9-10/r8.anchor: أي من غيري ثقة بي أو مطلقا

BAYDAWI-FULL:27:9-10/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:9-10/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:9-10/r9.claim: Messengers do not fear while receiving revelation because of their absorption in it, although they are the people most fearful of God.
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:9-10/r9.anchor: أي حين يوحى إليهم من فرط الاستغراق فإنهم أخوف الناس أي من الله تعالى

BAYDAWI-FULL:27:9-10/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:9-10/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:9-10/r10.claim: Alternatively, messengers have no fear of ending badly in God's presence.
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:9-10/r10.anchor: أو لا يكون لهم عندي سوء عاقبة فيخافون منه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r24.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r24.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r24.claim: Throwing the staff lets Moses witness God’s might and wisdom; alternatively, the command coordinates with the earlier blessing announcement.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r25.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r25.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r25.claim: The staff became a huge, exceptionally light and swift serpent, writhing as it pursued what it wanted.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r25.anchor: فصارت في الحال - بما أذنت به الفاء - حية عظيمة جدا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r26.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r26.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r26.claim: Jānn refers to a small snake in lightness and speed; this does not contradict the serpent’s large body.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r26.anchor: أي حية صغيرة في خفتها وسرعتها

BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r27.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r27.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r27.claim: Moses turned and fled from the serpent at great speed.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r27.anchor: اي التفت هاربا منها مسرعا جدا لقوله

BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r28.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r28.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r28.claim: He did not turn back, hesitate in fleeing, or look behind him.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r28.anchor: أي لم يرجع على عقبه , ولم يتردد في الجد في الهرب

BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r29.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r29.speaker: المحكم
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r29.claim: Al-Muḥkam gives ʿaqaba on someone the sense of turning back, and ʿaqaba in a matter the sense of persisting in pursuit.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r29.anchor: تردد في طلبه مجدا - هذا في ترتيب المحكم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r30.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r30.speaker: القاموس
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r30.claim: Al-Qāmūs gives taʿqīb the sense of looking back.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r31.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r31.speaker: القزاز
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r31.claim: Al-Qazzāz’s dictionary defines ʿaqaba as turning back after departing.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r31.anchor: وقال القزاز في ديوانه : عقب - إذا انصرف راجعا فهو معقب

BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r32.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r32.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r32.claim: God answers Moses’ fear with reassurance and a promise of safety.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r32.anchor: ولما تشوفت النفس غلى ما قيل له عند هذه الحالة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r33.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r33.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r33.claim: “In My presence” means the extraordinary setting and time of revelation.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r33.anchor: أي في الموضع الذي هو من غرائب نواقض العادات

BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r34.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r34.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r34.claim: Messengers are protected from injustice, and only a wrongdoer fears a just ruler.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r34.anchor: ولا يخاف من الملك العدل إلا ظالم

DURR-FULL:v6p341/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p341/r9.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v6p341/r9.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the staff shook because it had become a serpent moving along.
DURR-FULL:v6p341/r9.anchor: عن ابن جريج في قوله {فلما رآها تهتز كأنها جان} قال: حين تحولت حية تسعى

DURR-FULL:v6p342/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p342/r1.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v6p342/r1.claim: Mujahid says Moses did not turn back; one who sinned then changed to good repented of his wrongdoing and evil deed.
DURR-FULL:v6p342/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {ولم يعقب يا موسى} قال: لم يرجع وفي قوله {إلا من ظلم ثم بدل حسنا بعد سوء} قال: ثم تاب من بعد ظلمه واساءته

DURR-FULL:v6p342/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p342/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p342/r2.claim: Qatada says Moses ran away and did not look back.
DURR-FULL:v6p342/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {ولى مدبرا} قال: فارا {ولم يعقب} قال: لم يلتفت

DURR-FULL:v6p342/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p342/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p342/r3.claim: Qatada glosses ladayya as with Me.
DURR-FULL:v6p342/r3.anchor: وفي قوله {لا يخاف لدي} قال: عندي

DURR-FULL:v6p342/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p342/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p342/r4.claim: Qatada says God grants no wrongdoer safety except through repentance and good action after evil, for God is forgiving and merciful.
DURR-FULL:v6p342/r4.anchor: وفي قوله {إلا من ظلم} قال: إن الله لم يجز ظالما ثم عاد الله بعائدته وبرحمته

DURR-FULL:v6p342/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p342/r5.speaker: ميمون
DURR-FULL:v6p342/r5.claim: Maymun says that a wrongdoer has no security with God until he repents.
DURR-FULL:v6p342/r5.anchor: عن ميمون قال: إن الله قال لموسى {إني لا يخاف لدي المرسلون إلا من ظلم} وليس للظالم عندي أمان حتى يتوب

DURR-FULL:v6p342/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p342/r6.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
DURR-FULL:v6p342/r6.claim: Zayd b. Aslam is reported reading the exception clause.
DURR-FULL:v6p342/r6.anchor: عن زيد بن أسلم أنه قرأ {إلا من ظلم}

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2847#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2847#2/r1.speaker: وهب
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2847#2/r1.claim: Wahb says Moses understood the command as “abandon it” and cast down the staff as if rejecting it.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2847#2/r1.anchor: سمعت وهبا قال : فقال له الرب عز وجل ، القها يا موسى فظن موسى انه يقول ارفضها فالقاها على وجه الرفض .

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2847#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2847#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2847#2/r2.claim: An angel gave Moses the staff as he set out for Midian; it lit his nights, brought up plants when he struck the ground, and shook leaves for his flock.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2847#2/r2.anchor: عن قتادة ، عن ابن عباس ، في عصا موسى قال : تلك العصا اعطاه اياها ملك من الملائكة لما ان توجه إلى مدين

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2847#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2847#2/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2847#2/r3.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr gives Moses’ staff the name Masha.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2847#2/r3.anchor: عن جعفر ، عن سعيد بن جبير ، عن ابن عباس ، قال : كان اسم عصا موسى ماشا .

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2847#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2847#2/r4.speaker: ابن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2847#2/r4.claim: Ibn Jubayr says Moses’ staff was made of boxthorn (ʿawsaj).
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2847#2/r4.anchor: عن مسعود بن مالك ، عن ابن جبير قال : كانت عصا موسى عليه السلام من عوسج .

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2847#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2847#2/r5.speaker: وهب
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2847#2/r5.claim: Wahb depicts the transformed staff as an enormous serpent that swallowed a boulder, tore up a tree, and had fiery eyes, hair-like ridges, and snapping fangs; Moses fled without looking back.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2847#2/r5.anchor: قال : سمعت وهبا يقول : ثم حانت منه نظرة ، فاذا باعظم ثعبان نظر اليه الناظرون يدب يلتمس

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2847#2/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2847#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2847#2/r6.claim: Mujahid glosses “he did not look back” as “he did not return.”
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2847#2/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد قوله : ولم يعقب لم يرجع .

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2847#2/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2847#2/r7.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2847#2/r7.claim: Al-Suddi glosses the phrase as Moses not waiting.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2847#2/r7.anchor: عن السدي ولم يعقب لم ينتظر .

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2848/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2848/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2848/r1.claim: Qatada glosses the phrase as Moses not turning around.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2848/r1.anchor: عن قتادة ولم يعقب : اي لم يلتفت .

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2848/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2848/r2.speaker: وهب
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2848/r2.claim: Wahb says Moses ran far, then remembered his Lord and stopped out of shame; the call summoned him back to where he had been.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2848/r2.anchor: قال : سمعت وهبا يقول : فلما عاين ذلك موسى ولى مدبرا ولم يعقب ، فذهب حتى امعن وراى انه قد اعجز الحية ثم ذكر ربه

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2848/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2848/r3.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2848/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd says Moses panicked at the serpent and did not calm at reassurance; only when told the staff would return to its former state did he turn, find it a staff, and take it, later controlling it against Pharaoh.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2848/r3.anchor: سمعت عبد الرحمن بن زيد في قوله : ولم يعقب يا موسى لا تخف قال : لما القى العصا صارت حية

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2848/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2848/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2848/r4.claim: Qatada explains “with Me” as “in My presence.”
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2848/r4.anchor: عن قتادة قوله : لدي المرسلون اي عندي المرسلون .

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p250#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p250#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p250#2/r1.claim: God gave Moses the two commands to train him in using the signs.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p250#2/r1.anchor: أمره الله عز وجل بهذين الأمرين تدريبا له في استعمالهما

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p250#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p250#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p250#2/r2.claim: The narrative omits the act of throwing the staff; the implied words are “so he cast the staff.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p250#2/r2.anchor: وفي الكلام حذف تقديره فألقى العصا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p250#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p250#2/r3.speaker: بعض القراء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p250#2/r3.claim: Some readers pronounce raaʾaha with imāla.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p250#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p250#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p250#2/r4.claim: Al-jānn means snakes, named for concealing themselves.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p250#2/r4.anchor: و «الجان» الحيات لأنها تجن أنفسها أي تسترها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p250#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p250#2/r5.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p250#2/r5.claim: A group says al-jānn are small snakes, while Moses’ staff became a great serpent.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p250#2/r5.anchor:
وقالت فرقة:
الجان صغار الحيات وعصا موسى صارت حية ثعبانا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p250#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p250#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p250#2/r6.claim: The great serpent resembled a small snake in its quick movement, since smaller snakes move faster.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p250#2/r6.anchor: شبهت ب «الجان» في سرعة الاضطراب، لأن الصغار أكثر حركة من الكبار

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p250#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p250#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p250#2/r7.claim: Either way, God created life in the staff and changed its properties so it became a serpent.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p250#2/r7.anchor: وعلى كل قول فإن الله خلق في العصا حياة وغير أوصافها وأعراضها فصارت حية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p250#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p250#2/r8.speaker: الحسن والزهري وعمرو بن عبيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p250#2/r8.claim: Al-Hasan, al-Zuhrī, and ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd read jān with hamza.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p250#2/r8.anchor: وقرأ الحسن والزهري وعمرو بن عبيد «جأن» بالهمز

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p250#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p250#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p250#2/r9.claim: Moses fled at the terrifying sight.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p250#2/r9.anchor: فلما أبصر موسى عليه السلام هول ذلك المنظر ولى فارا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p250#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p250#2/r10.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p250#2/r10.claim: Mujāhid says Moses did not return.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p250#2/r10.anchor: قال مجاهد ولم يرجع وقال قتادة: ولم يلتفت

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p250#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p250#2/r11.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p250#2/r11.claim: Qatāda says Moses did not look back.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p250#2/r11.anchor: قال مجاهد ولم يرجع وقال قتادة: ولم يلتفت

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p250#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p250#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p250#2/r12.claim: A person ʿaqqaba after turning away if he turns his body or face back toward the matter, as if on his heels.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p250#2/r12.anchor: و «عقب» الرجل إذا ولى عن أمر ثم صرف بدنه أو وجهه إليه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p250#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p250#2/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p250#2/r13.claim: God reassures Moses that His chosen messengers do not fear in His presence or with Him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p250#2/r13.anchor: وناداه الله مؤنسا ومقويا على الأمر: يا موسى لا تخف فإن رسلي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p250#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p250#2/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p250#2/r14.claim: Moses took the snake, which returned to a staff; this became familiar to him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p250#2/r14.anchor: فأخذ موسى الحية فرجعت عصا ثم صارت له عادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p156#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p156#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p156#2/r1.claim: The verse omits the action: Moses cast the staff and it became a serpent.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p156#2/r1.anchor: في الآية محذوف تقديره فألقاها فصارت حية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p156#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p156#2/r2.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p156#2/r2.claim: Al-Farra says jann is a snake neither large nor small.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p156#2/r2.anchor: قال الفراء الجان الحية التي ليست بالعظيمة ولا بالصغيرة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p156#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p156#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p156#2/r3.claim: Qatada interprets لم يعقب as not looking back.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p156#2/r3.anchor: فيه قولان أحدهما لم يلتفت قاله قتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p156#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p156#2/r4.speaker: ابن قتيبة والزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p156#2/r4.claim: Ibn Qutayba and al-Zajjaj interpret it as not returning; Ibn Qutayba derives it from عقب.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p156#2/r4.anchor: والثاني لم يرجع قاله ابن قتيبة والزجاج قال ابن قتيبة وأهل النظر يرون أنه مأخوذ من العقب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p156#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p156#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p156#2/r5.claim: God says that messengers do not fear in His presence.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p156#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p156#2/r6.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p156#2/r6.claim: Another view places this reassurance where God reveals to the messengers.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p156#2/r6.anchor: وقيل المراد في الموضع الذي يوحي إليهم فيه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p156#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p156#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p156#2/r7.claim: One whom God has secured from punishment through prophethood should not fear a snake.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p156#2/r7.anchor: فكأنه نبهه على أن من آمنه الله بالنبوة من عذابه لا ينبغي أن يخاف من حية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p180/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p180/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p180/r3.claim: God commands Moses to drop his staff as a clear proof that God freely chooses and has power over everything.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p180/r3.anchor: ثم أمره أن يلقي عصاه من يده؛ ليظهر له دليلا واضحا على أنه الفاعل المختار، القادر على كل شيء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p180/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p180/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p180/r4.claim: The staff immediately became an enormous, terrifying serpent that moved with great speed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p180/r4.anchor: انقلبت في الحال حية عظيمة هائلة في غاية الكبر، وسرعة الحركة مع ذلك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p180/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p180/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p180/r5.claim: A jann is a kind of snake distinguished by especially fast, restless movement; Ibn Kathir notes a hadith prohibiting killing house snakes.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p180/r5.anchor: والجان: ضرب من الحيات، أسرعه حركة، وأكثره اضطرابا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p180/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p180/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p180/r6.claim: Moses ran away without looking back because he was intensely frightened.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p180/r6.anchor: أي: لم يلتفت من شدة فرقه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p180/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p180/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p180/r7.claim: God tells Moses not to fear what he sees because God intends to choose him as a messenger and make him an honored prophet.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p180/r7.anchor: فإني أريد أن أصطفيك رسولا وأجعلك نبيا وجيها

JISHUMI:v8p5409/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5409/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5409/r4.claim: Jānn is a small snake, named from concealment (ijtinān).
JISHUMI:v8p5409/r4.anchor: والجان: الحية الصغيرة، أخذت من الاجتنان، وهو الاستتار

JISHUMI:v8p5409/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5409/r5.speaker: الفراء
JISHUMI:v8p5409/r5.claim: Al-Farra says a jānn is a snake between small and large.
JISHUMI:v8p5409/r5.anchor: وقال الفراء: هي حية بين الصغيرة والكبيرة.

JISHUMI:v8p5409/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5409/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5409/r6.claim: One explanation says lam yuʿaqqib means he did not return; each muʿaqqib is someone who comes back.
JISHUMI:v8p5409/r6.anchor: (لم يعقب) قيل: لم يرجع، قال: سمي كل معقب راجع

JISHUMI:v8p5409/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5409/r7.speaker: عمر
JISHUMI:v8p5409/r7.claim: A report about Umar says he would cycle the armies each year, recalling one contingent and dispatching another to take its turn.
JISHUMI:v8p5409/r7.anchor: وفي حديث عمر: (كان يعقب الجيوش في كل عام) أي: يرد فوجا، ويبعث آخرين

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r16.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r16.claim: One view says jann is a small snake, named for its hiding and concealment.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r16.anchor: أحدهما : أن الجان الحية الصغيرة , سميت بذلك لاجتنانها واستتارها .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r17.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r17.claim: Another view takes jann as a devil from the jinn, since frightening things are likened to Satan.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r17.anchor: والثاني : أنه أراد بالجان الشيطان من الجن , لأنهم يشبهون كل ما استهولوه بالشيطان

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r18.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r18.claim: Although the simile names a small jann, Moses's staff became a huge serpent, as the accounts in 7:107 and 26:33 clarify.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r18.anchor: وقد كان انقلاب العصا إلى أعظم الحيات لا إلى أصغرها , كما قال تعالى : ^ { فإذا هي ثعبان مبين }

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r19.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r19.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says an angel gave Moses the staff when he set out for Midian and that it was called masha.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r19.anchor: قال عبد الله بن عباس : وكانت العصا قد أعطاه إياها ملك من الملائكة حين توجه إلى مدين وكان اسمها : ما شاء

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r20.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r20.speaker: ابن جبير
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r20.claim: Ibn Jubayr says the staff was made of boxthorn.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r20.anchor: قال ابن جبير : وكانت من عوسج .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r21.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r21.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r21.claim: Mujahid says lam yuʿaqqib means that Moses did not return; Qutrub derives the word from the heel.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r21.anchor: أحدها : ولم يرجع , قاله مجاهد , قال قطرب : مأخوذ من العقب .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r22.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r22.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r22.claim: Al-Suddi says Moses did not wait.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r23.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r23.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r23.claim: Qatada says Moses did not look back.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r24.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r24.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r24.claim: He also suggests it could mean Moses stayed put rather than walking, since walking follows its starting movement by placing the heel before the foot.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r24.anchor: في المشيء معقب لابتدائه بوضع عقبة قبل قدمه .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r25.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r25.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r25.claim: One explanation restricts the assurance to the place where revelation comes, since messengers otherwise fear God more than others.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r25.anchor: قيل إنه أراد في الموضع الذي يوحى فيه إليهم , ولا فالمرسلون من الله أخوف .

MUJAHID:v2p469#3/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p469#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p469#3/r1.claim: Mujahid glosses “he did not turn back” as “he did not return.”
MUJAHID:v2p469#3/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد ﴿ ولم يعقب ﴾ قال يقول لم يرجع

MUQATIL:27:7-10/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:27:7-10/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:27:7-10/r7.claim: The staff’s trembling means it moved, and its appearance like a jinn means it looked like a snake.
MUQATIL:27:7-10/r7.anchor: { وألق عصاك فلما رآها تهتز } يعنى تحرك { كأنها جآن } يعنى كأنها كانت حية

MUQATIL:27:7-10/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:27:7-10/r8.speaker: author
MUQATIL:27:7-10/r8.claim: Moses fled in fear of the snake and did not turn back; God told him not to fear, since messengers do not fear in His presence.
MUQATIL:27:7-10/r8.anchor: { ولى مدبرا } من الخوف من الحية { ولم يعقب } يعنى ولم يرجع

NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#5/r1.claim: Moses is told to throw his staff so he will recognize the miracle and find reassurance in it; the command is coordinated with the blessing pronouncement.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#5/r1.anchor: لتعلم معجزتك فتأنس بها وهو عطف على بورك

NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#5/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#5/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#5/r2.claim: Both the blessing and throwing the staff explain what Moses was called to hear; al-Qasas puts the command after the call to Moses, repeating the explanatory particle.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#5/r2.anchor: لأن المعنى نودى أن بورك من في النار وأن ألق عصاك كلاهما تفسير لنودى

NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#5/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#5/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#5/r3.claim: Tahtazzu is a circumstantial clause attached to the object pronoun in raʾāhā.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#5/r3.anchor: تتحرك حال من الهاء في رآها

NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#5/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#5/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#5/r4.claim: A jan is a small snake.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#5/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#5/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#5/r5.claim: The phrase as though it were a small snake is a circumstantial clause of the pronoun in tahtazzu.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#5/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#5/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#5/r6.claim: Moses turned away and fled, putting his back to the snake out of fear that it would spring on him.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#5/r6.anchor: ﴿ ولي ﴾ موسى ﴿ مدبرا ﴾ أدبر عنها وجعلها تلى ظهره خوفا من ثوب الحية عليه

NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#5/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#5/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#5/r7.claim: Lam yuʿaqqib means he did not look back or did not return; the idiom can describe someone who returns to fight after fleeing.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#5/r7.anchor: ولم يلتفت أو لم يرجع يقال قد عقب فلان إذا رجع يقاتل بعد أن ولى

NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#5/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#5/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#5/r8.claim: One sense is that messengers do not fear while God is addressing them.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#5/r8.anchor: أي لا يخاف عندي المرسلون حال خطابي اياهم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#5/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#5/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#5/r9.claim: Alternatively, messengers do not fear anyone besides God.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#5/r9.anchor: أو لا يخاف لدى المرسلون من غيري

QURTUBI-FULL:27:8-10/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8-10/r9.speaker: وهب بن منبه
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8-10/r9.claim: Wahb says Moses thought God was ordering him to discard his staff.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8-10/r9.anchor: قال وهب بن منبه: ظن موسى أن الله أمره أن يرفضها فرفضها

QURTUBI-FULL:27:10-11/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:10-11/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:27:10-11/r1.claim: The sign lets Moses recognize that the speaker is God and that he is God’s messenger; each prophet needs a personal sign of prophethood.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:10-11/r1.anchor: وقيل: إنما قال له ذلك ليعلم موسى أن المكلم له هو الله، وأن موسى رسوله

QURTUBI-FULL:27:10-11/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:10-11/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:27:10-11/r2.claim: The account omits that Moses threw the staff from his hand; it became a moving serpent like a jān.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:10-11/r2.anchor: وفي الآية حذف: أي وألق عصاك فألقاها من يده فصارت حية تهتز كأنها جان

QURTUBI-FULL:27:10-11/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:10-11/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:27:10-11/r3.claim: A jān is a small, light-bodied snake.

QURTUBI-FULL:27:10-11/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:10-11/r4.speaker: الكلبي
QURTUBI-FULL:27:10-11/r4.claim: Al-Kalbī says the snake was neither small nor large.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:10-11/r4.anchor: وقال الكلبي: لا صغيرة ولا كبيرة

QURTUBI-FULL:27:10-11/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:10-11/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:27:10-11/r5.claim: One account says it first became small, then grew large once Moses became accustomed to it.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:10-11/r5.anchor: وقيل: إنها قلبت له أولا حية صغيرة فلما أنس منها قلبت حية كبيرة

QURTUBI-FULL:27:10-11/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:10-11/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:27:10-11/r6.claim: Another account says it changed from a small snake to a female serpent and then a large male thُʿbān.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:10-11/r6.anchor: وقيل: انقلبت مرة حية صغيرة، ومرة حية تسعى وهي الأنثى، ومرة ثعبانا وهو الذكر الكبير من الحيات

QURTUBI-FULL:27:10-11/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:10-11/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:27:10-11/r7.claim: A further account describes one huge snake with a thُʿbān’s size but a jān’s lightness and quick movement.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:10-11/r7.anchor: وقيل: المعنى انقلبت ثعبانا تهتز كأنها جان لها عظم الثعبان وخفة الجان واهتزازه

QURTUBI-FULL:27:10-11/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:10-11/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:27:10-11/r8.claim: The plural of jān is jinān, as in the prophetic prohibition against killing snakes in houses.

QURTUBI-FULL:27:10-11/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:10-11/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:27:10-11/r9.claim: Moses fled in fear, as is natural for human beings.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:10-11/r9.anchor: { ولى مدبرا } خائفا على عادة البشر

QURTUBI-FULL:27:10-11/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:10-11/r10.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:27:10-11/r10.claim: Mujāhid explains لم يعقب as “he did not return.”
QURTUBI-FULL:27:10-11/r10.anchor: { ولم يعقب } أي لم يرجع قاله مجاهد

QURTUBI-FULL:27:10-11/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:10-11/r11.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:27:10-11/r11.claim: Qatāda explains it as “he did not look back.”

QURTUBI-FULL:27:10-11/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:10-11/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:27:10-11/r12.claim: The reassurance tells Moses not to fear harm from the snake.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:10-11/r12.anchor: { يموسى لا تخف } أي من الحية وضررها

QURTUBI-FULL:27:10-11/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:10-11/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:27:10-11/r13.claim: One parsing ends the sentence here and treats إلا من ظلم as a disconnected exception.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:10-11/r13.anchor: وتم الكلام ثم استثنى استثناء منقطعا فقال: { إلا من ظلم }

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p269#2/r6.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p269#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p269#2/r6.claim: Kasra on the rāʾ and hamza in the example is called imālat al-imāla.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p269#2/r6.anchor: فأما كسر الراء والهمزة فتسمى إمالة الإمالة
